content:
✅ Approved the contribution.
Comment: A couple of times I covered several test cases with one change and some test cases required multiple changes, so I guess there could be more test cases, but it's a minor nitpick, I think there's already a lot of test cases.
Overall interesting puzzle and good description/test cases, didn't find any issues.
Although I would probably make it a hard puzzle instead of medium, but of course it's subjective.
Minor naming issue: "Multiple requested targets" should probably use "required" which is already used in puzzle description, so "Multiple required targets"

Goal
* "Everything after (the colon) is a whitespace-separated list" is not quite accurate. Please describe it consistently with the actual syntax (a colon followed by a space).

* Built-in macros table: Please move "in definition order" onto a separate line. The current table row is truncated on narrower browser windows.

* "Either list may be empty" contradicts the syntax shown, which always contains at least one target before the colon.

* There are currently no test cases that require handling of multiple targets before the colon. If rule lines are always single-target, please remove the multi-target explanation for simplicity. Otherwise, please add test cases that exercise multi-target rules.

* Please standardise the terms. Currently several similar or undefined terms are used:

  • rules, rule lines
  • actions, action lines
  • definitions
  • definition action lines

* "If no targets are requested" is unclear because the term "requested" is never mentioned elsewhere. Presumably this corresponds to nTargets = 0, but the Input section doesn't state that explicitly.

* Consider replacing the term "dependency graph" (used twice in the statement) with a direct description of the requirement (e.g. "all target dependencies are checked for cycles before building") for easier understanding.

* Timestamps ignored: Consider moving this point to the end as a note rather than including it among the core build rules.

* Formatting:
  • "targets", "prerequisites", "actions", "rules", "action lines", "comments" and "default target" in <<bold>> instead of as {{constants}}

  • ":", "TAB" and "#" as {{constants}} instead of [[variables]].
 
Input / Constraints
* Please align the variable names with those used in the stub generator.

Output
* <If a circular dependency is detected:>: Please format ">" in <<bold>>.

* Please format "A single line", "One line per action executed" and "Final line" in <<bold>> and remove the surrounding "<" and ">".

* Please format "[Circular dependencies detected]" and "[Build complete]" as {{constants}}.

* A single line already implies that only one line should be output, so the phrase "— no action lines (etc.) are output" is unnecessary. Please remove it for clarity.

Constraints
* Please add a constraint for every input in the same order as it appears in the Input section:

  • integer input: lower and upper bounds.

  • string input: minimum and maximum lengths.

* Please state targets and prerequisite names do not contain spaces or {{#}} characters.

* Please use bounds that better reflect the actual test cases, e.g. 10 instead of 1000.

Stub generator
* Please change Line 2 to:
loopline nTargets target:word(10)

* Please replace 1024 and the above 10 with the upper bounds used in the Constraints section.

Cases
* Please remove trailing newlines from both the inputs and the outputs of all the cases.

* N is 0 in most cases.

* I'll review the cases in more detail once the statement is clearer.

Thanks.

Thanks much for feedback.  Addressing now.

I'm also thinking of adding a list of preexisting target names with timestamp values to the inputs, so that timestamp-dependent builds are part of the problem, which would make it more interesting than a standard dependency graph. Do you think that's a bad idea?

Thank you! Nice solution…

I’m having some trouble getting moderators to lo review it, hopefully I can get a couple more approvals in the next two weeks.
Thank you for the feedback.  Fixed...

Thanks for your feedback and approval. I agree that test cases could be more focussed, but as you say there are a lot of tests (the contribution submission network request already takes more than 2 minutes to complete and generates a timeout error at the cloudflare load balancer) and there are too many criteria to only test one criterion per test. I hope at least that all criteria are covered…

You seem to have some insight into why the submission process can take so long. I've been wondering about that myself, as even very simple updates to straightforward puzzles can take quite a while and sometimes still end up failing with an error. That really shouldn't be happening. If you have any idea what's causing it, it'd be great if you could share your insights with the CG team; it might help them identify and fix the underlying issue.

Yes, I’ve been building a command line tool to help with managing, debugging, and submitting puzzles and contributions—I will share it when it is stable

The problem is definitely due to the fact that there is a single api for updating a contribution, and it does not return until every single test case (both local user tests and server validator tests) has been run against your reference solution and are confirmed to pass. The api fails if your tests don’t pass. 

Running a test server side is pretty heavyweight, it has to create a sandbox (a docker container or VM) with the right language support, inject your solution, compile and launch  your solution, and read the results. It seems slower for updating a contribution than submitting a puzzle solution—for one thing there are twice as many tests to run, but it may also be true that once a contribution is approved, the validation sandbox for the puzzle is persisted/optimized so it can spin up more quickly. 

The right solution to the timeout problem is to break the api into two parts—the first one would start the contribution update and put it into a pending state and return immediately. There would be a second api to poll for completion of the update and success/failure. That would solve the current timeout problem. Note that is already the way puzzle submission works, so they obviously know about the underlying problem. 

That wouldn’t speed up the time required to update a contribution, but it would eliminate the timeout problem. To speed it up, the simplest thing they could do is run all the tests in parallel. They may have considered that idea and rejected it because it causes brief bursts of increased resource usage (CPU and RAM). It’s also reasonable that optimizing the contribution experience isn’t at the top of their priority list, since the vast majority of users don’t make contributions.

Thank you very much for your detailed explanation.

I've had a couple of previous observations that may add a bit more detail:

* If I only change metadata (for example, the statement, test case names or ordering), the update completes almost immediately.

* If I modify only some of the test cases, only those cases are revalidated.

These observations suggest that the backend is already smart enough to avoid rerunning validation when it isn't necessary, and to revalidate only the affected cases. That said, even updating a single test case can still fail due to the timeout.

What do you think the best next step is? If you think it's appropriate, I'm happy to pass your findings on to the CG team. Would you prefer that I share your Discord ID so they can contact you directly, or would you rather I simply refer them to your message here? I should mention that I won't have the technical background to answer any follow-up questions they might have.

Right, I should have been more detailed… the service seem smart enough to only run test cases that have not been verified. If the solution source code changes it reruns all tests. If only test cases change, it only runs those that change. If neither source code nor test cases change, it doesn’t run any tests…. That is just a guess based on observations, of course. 

I’m happy to have you share with them; also happy to communicate with them directly if they like. If there is anything I can do to help, please let me know…

Thanks. I think that could work, but a few things come to mind.

The current (unrevised) Goal section is already around 4.2k characters, with a 5k limit. So, the feasibility of adding timestamps will depend on how much additional explanation is needed.

From a puzzle-design perspective, differentiating it from existing dependency-graph-style puzzles is not a bad idea, given that there's already a somewhat similar puzzle involving library dependencies, cycle detection, and lexicographic tie-breaking/reordering (see https://www.codingame.com/training/easy/library-dependencies ).

That said, it depends on the complexity level you're aiming for. Adding timestamps could make the puzzle more interesting and make the puzzle a closer simulation of make-style build behaviour, but it'd also move the puzzle away from being a relatively straightforward graph problem and increase both implementation and statement complexity.
OK, I think I have addressed most of your concerns, and I have added timestamps as well, and improved the test cases. Let me know what you think and if I should open it for approval...
Thanks for the update. I'll review the contribution as soon as I can, and should be able to get back to you by next Tuesday at the latest.

Goal
* First paragraph: The phrase "build outdated or missing target files" sounds odd. Consider rewording it to indicate that a target file is (re)built if it is outdated or missing, or simply omit "outdated or missing".

* Whitespace handling is described in both the Whitespace and Actions sections. Consider avoiding the duplication:

  • Replace "Except for the special case of a TAB at the start of a line" with "After using {{TAB}}s to identify actions (see below), {{TAB}}s".

  • Replace "The TAB and any additional leading/trailing whitespace is removed, and the line is interpreted as" with "Applying the whitespace rules above to the line yields".

* Please correct the typo: he resulting => the resulting.

* Consider avoiding the new term "default target" and replacing "the default target … is used" with "the first <<target>> in the first <<rule>> of the Makefile is treated as the <<required target>>".

* In the example, consider revising the input order to better illustrate:

  • the lexicographically smaller name main.o is built first

  • the prerequisites in their given rule order, not the order they were built

Input
* Please change the first "One Line" to "Line 1", and the other two occurrences to "Next line".

* Please replace "If cmdArgs is empty, the default target is the required target" with "or an empty line", since the behaviour is already explained in the Goal section (if you adopt the suggestion above).

* "Syntax rules are described above" may be removed.

Output
* Please format "A single line" in <<bold>>.

* Please format "One line per action executed" in <<bold>> and remove the surrounding "<" and ">".

* Please format "Final line" in <<bold>>.

* Please format "[Circular dependencies detected]" and "[Build complete]" as {{constants}} instead of using ```monospace``` formatting.

Constraints
* Please specify lower bounds for nLines, nFiles, len(cmdArgs) and len(makefileLine).

* Please change "len" to "length" (3 times).

* Please change 10^9 to 1000.

* Please change 200 to 100 (twice).

* Please reorder the first six constraints to match the order of items in the Input section.

* Please reorder the final six constraints so that related ones (e.g. all constraints related to actions) are grouped together as much as possible.

Stub generator
* Line 2: Please change 200 to 20.

* Line 3 & Line 5: Please change 200 to 100.

Cases
* Please remove trailing newlines from both the inputs and the outputs of all cases.

* nFiles = 0 in 4 tests and no validators. Please modify the cases so that there are equal numbers of tests and validators with nFiles = 0.

* Targets that share the same prerequisites seem to appear in validators only, but not in any tests.

* Please split the final pair of test and validator into two pairs, as they cover entirely different scenarios.

* Please ensure that every specification in the Goal section is covered by at least one test and at least one validator.

Thanks.
All feedback sounds reasonable, will address. Thanks for the time you put in reviewing…
OK, all feedback addressed.  Most testcases rewritten, and there are now 12 pairs of tests.

The statement is mostly fine; just some minor points left. Focusing more on the cases.

Goal
* Whitespace: Please add "{{TAB}}," after "(see below)".

* $^: Consider replacing "in rule definition order" with "preserving their order in the rule" for clarity.

* Build semantics

  • Consider replacing "is used" with "is treated as the <<required target>>" for clarity.

  • Please replace "dependency cycle" with "circular dependency" to match the output terminology.

Goal - Rules / Cases
* Please either:

  • Add "distinct" after "zero or more" if rules with duplicate prerequisites are disallowed or never tested, or

  • Add cases with such rules.

* Please either:

  • Adopt the syntax already used in the cases (no whitespace + ":" + [whitespace when prerequisites exist]), and remove "Whitespace adjacent to the : is optional.", or

  • Modify cases to cover:
    - Whitespace before colon.
    - No whitespace after colon.

Output
* Please remove the stray ">" after "action executed:".

Constraints
* Please either change the lower bound for length(makefileLine) from 0 to 1, or modify existing cases to include blank lines.

* Please add a general validity guarantee for all inputs except circular dependencies. (I'm thinking of no unexplained situations like "the rule associated with a `$<` has no prerequisites".)

Stub generator
* Line 2: Please change 20 to 100 to match the constraints.

Cases
* Please remove trailing newlines from both the inputs and the outputs of all cases.

* Pair 2: Test 2 skips building all targets while Validator 2 doesn't. Please split them into separate pairs.

* Comments after a TAB appear in a validator only. Please add the same style of a comment to a test.

* If comments may appear at the end of rules, please include the following in at least one test and at least one validator:

  • Comment in a rule with prerequisites.

  • Comment in a rule without prerequisites.

* Multi-target rule with same-age out-of-date check: The scenario of multiple targets defined in a single rule being built in a different order than their appearance in that rule is covered in the validator only. Please add the same scenario to the test.

* Same target in multiple rules: The "same target in multiple rules containing the same prerequisite" scenario appears in the test only. Please add the same scenario to the validator.

* If valid, please modify or add cases where a target appears in multiple rules, and one of those rules is also a multi-target rule.

* Are these covered in any cases?

  • A preexisting file with no prerequisites is up to date

  • A target that has no actions produces no output, but its prerequisites are still built.

* It seems "Multiple action lines per rule" should appear before "All features".

* Please add a new pair of highly comprehensive cases (more comprehensive than "All features"), with a single required target in [[cmdArgs]], and covering as many as possible the scenarios featured in the existing cases.

Thanks.

Sorry for the slow response. I've done my best to address all your concerns, including rewriting virtually all of the tests and cross checking them against a long list of fine-grained test criteria for coverage.  Let me know what you think.

BTW, I got tired of copy/pasting into the web form so I made a whole python client for managing contributions and submitting them; it even launches a chromium browser for you to log in, and extracts the rememberMe and cgSession cookies for authorization. Also handles upload of the cover image file. I started with https://github.com/takos22/codingame but at this point I've made far too many changes for a pull request (I don't like packages that aren't properly type hinted) and their clever trick to make a single codebase for sync/async fundamentally breaks static linting. I don't know if you all have an interest in a formal client SDK but its a good starting point.

Thanks for the update! I can see you've put a lot of work into this revision. The statement is clearer now, and I appreciate the effort that went into rewriting the tests and systematically checking their coverage. I think the puzzle is in very good shape now.

Also, that contribution client sounds really nice! I imagine other contributors would find it useful too. How about sharing the link on the forum and/or Discord?

Below is the updated list of points, some of which were raised in my previous comment.

Constraints
* Consider adding:
{{$<}} is only associated with a rule having at least one prerequisite.

(By comparison, I noticed that $^ is associated with a rule with no prerequisites in the final case pair, so no corresponding constraint is needed.)

Cases
* Please remove trailing newlines from both the inputs and the outputs of all cases.

* The current version removes the following case from the previous version. Please restore it as part of a new case pair immediately after the current Pair 3, "Single rule with no actions" (without removing the existing pair).

Input
4
src.c 50
main.o 100
util.o 100
program 200

6
program: main.o util.o
	link $^ -o $@
main.o: src.c
	cc -c $< -o $@
util.o: src.c
	cc -c $< -o $@

Output
[Build complete]

* Comments after a TAB appear in one validator (Built-in macros and comments (Validator 7)) only. Please add comments in the same style to Test 7, the final test, and the final validator.

* Multi-target rule with same-age staleness (Pair 8): The revised test is closer to the validator, but it still doesn't verify the build-order requirement. Please revise it so that `util.o` also needs to be built.

* Please modify the "Cycle detection" cases (Pair 11) so that the circular dependency is among the required targets only.

* Please add a separate case pair where the circular dependency exists only among targets that are *not* built.

* Please modify the final test, the final validator, and at least one other case pair to include:

  • the syntax with no whitespace after colon in a rule.

  • a target appearing in multiple rules, where one of those rules is also a multi-target rule with distinct targets.

  • a scenario where `dep_time is None` in the `is_out_of_date` method (line 411) is triggered, if it's reachable under the current specification. (The condition is never true in the current cases.)

Thanks again.

Thank you!

For your one point about dep_time being None, that will never happen, since prerequisites are always built before is_out_of_date() is called, ensuring that all prerequisites have a timestamp. I will add an assertion to that effect in my reference solution.

I will address all other points.

Thanks again for such thoughtful feedback.

OK, Addressed each of your points, including the EOL on the final line of test files :-D.

I'm out of town for a few days so I went ahead and marked it ready for moderation, though I'm happy to address more issues as they arise.

Thanks much for your help!

Thank you for all the updates so far! I haven't noticed any significant issues with the current version, so I'm happy to leave it as is for now (and save a few minor suggestions for when modifications are absolutely necessary). I'll let you know if I spot anything later 🙂
A week in and no upvotes, downvotes, approvals, or rejections. At this rate it will die from disinterest.  Anything I should be doing to kick some reviews?

It's unfortunately like that for most contributions. Some can go through several 30-day review cycles before they're approved.

You could try promoting your contribution on CodinGame's Discord server. Either way, it usually takes a lot of patience.
